pages.name: Halves in three
pages.text: 6 ÷ 2 asks how many 2s fit in 6, and three do. 3 ÷ 1/2 asks the same with halves. Six fit along the 3 bars, so 3 ÷ 1/2 = 6.

pages.name: Quarters in two
pages.why: Each whole holds 4 quarters, so 2 wholes hold 8 of them. So 2 ÷ 1/4 = 8.

pages.name: Cable into tails
pages.text: Here 6 m of cable is cut into tails 3/4 m long. Counted along the tape, eight fit, so 6 ÷ 3/4 = 8.

pages.name: Tails from 3 m
pages.task: How many 3/4 m tails can you cut from 3 m of cable? Cut them one at a time.
pages.why: 3 m is twelve quarter-metres, and each tail takes three of them. So 4 tails fit, and 3 ÷ 3/4 = 4.

pages.name: Why you flip
pages.text: A metre is 4 quarters and a tail takes 3, so a metre holds 4/3 tails. Six metres hold 6 × 4/3 = 8. So dividing by 3/4 is multiplying by 3/4 with its top and bottom swapped, its [[reciprocal]].

pages.name: Less than one fits
pages.why: Flip the 3/4 to 4/3, so 1/2 × 4/3 = 4/6 = 2/3. Two of the piece's 3 quarters fit in the half, which is 2/3 of it.

pages.name: Smaller pieces, more of them
pages.text: The smaller the piece, the more of them fit. Divide an amount above 0 by a number more than 1 and you get less. Divide it by a fraction between 0 and 1 and you get more.

pages.name: Bigger than 10
pages.task: Which of these is bigger than 10?
pages.why: Dividing by 1/2 counts the halves in 10, and there are 20. Dividing by 2 and taking half of 10 both give 5.

pages.name: Tails from four and a half
pages.task: How many 3/4 m tails can you cut from 4 1/2 m of cable?
pages.why: 4 1/2 is 9/2, and 3/4 flipped is 4/3. So 9/2 × 4/3 = 36/6 = 6 tails.

pages.name: Three quarters by a half
pages.why: 1/2 flipped is 2/1, which is 2. So 3/4 × 2 = 6/4 = 1 1/2. One half fits in 3/4, and half of another.
